slot.brief: Two balls thrown vertically from the same point one after another meet at a common height; find the time interval between throws or the meeting height.

stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward at $15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. One second later, another is thrown upward from the same point at $25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. If $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, at what height do they meet?

verdicts.working: Let t be the time (s) after the first throw. Equating heights, 15t−5t² = 25(t−1)−5(t−1)² gives t=1.5 s. Their height is 15(1.5)−5(1.5)² = 11.25 m.

working:
Let $t$ be measured from the first throw: $y_1=15t-5t^2$, $y_2=25(t-1)-5(t-1)^2$.
$y_1=y_2\Rightarrow t=1.5$ s.
$y=15(1.5)-5(1.5)^2=11.25$ m.

Independent check: Let t be the time (s) after the first throw. Equating heights, 15t−5t² = 25(t−1)−5(t−1)² gives t=1.5 s. Their height is 15(1.5)−5(1.5)² = 11.25 m.
solution:
Taking $t$ from the first throw, the heights are $y_1=15t-5t^2$ and $y_2=25(t-1)-5(t-1)^2$.
$$y_1=y_2\Rightarrow t=1.5\text{ s},\qquad y=15(1.5)-5(1.5)^2=11.25\text{ m}$$
